title: Bimodality in pan-cancer proteomics reveals new opportunities for biomarker discovery.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC: no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no accessions, no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI. bioRxiv API: preprint 10.1101/2025.03.03.641218 (AstraZeneca, licence cc_no = no reuse licence). GitHub search found FayeJiang09/Bimodality_proteomics, but its contents and README return 404 (empty or inaccessible repo). No data table was opened.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 2401 tumour-associated bimodal proteins, the use of CPTAC (Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium) pan-cancer proteomics, the knowledge-graph analysis and the TROP2 case study all come from the abstract and search snippets only.

a1_downloadable.note: No supplement retrievable through Europe PMC (no PMCID), the authors' GitHub repo is empty or 404, and the preprint has no reuse licence. The underlying CPTAC data is open on the PDC (Proteomic Data Commons), but this paper's own bimodality calls were not found anywhere downloadable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The only paper-specific label (whether a protein is bimodal) would have to be rebuilt by rerunning the authors' bimodality model on CPTAC protein tables; it is not a column we could download.

a3_inputs_present.note: Not checked in files. The CPTAC protein abundance matrices are public, keyed by gene symbol.

a4_units_stated.note: Not checked. CPTAC harmonised tables are log2 ratios to a reference channel, according to CPTAC documentation and not this paper.

a5_enough_rows.note: The abstract reports 2401 bimodal proteins out of roughly 10k quantified (that total is not verified). Row count not seen.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No file to compare against the paper's 2401 count.

a8_label_provenance.note: The bimodal/not-bimodal label is the output of the authors' statistical mixture model, computed from the same expression values a model would use as features. Predicting it from those values is circular; predicting it from sequence would mean distilling their model.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (only if bimodality were predicted from sequence)

integration.partner_dataset: CPTAC PDC pan-cancer proteomics; Human Protein Atlas
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do proteins with bimodal tumour abundance share sequence or network features that would flag new patient-stratifying biomarkers? This would need the label to exist as a released table, and it does not.

controls.positive_control: TROP2 (TACSTD2) bimodal in colon adenocarcinoma, per the abstract
controls.external_validation: None found apart from RNA-based bimodality lists from earlier work, which were not retrieved

honest_claim_h3: At best: reproduces the authors' mixture-model bimodality calls on CPTAC tumours. That is a statistical summary of the input data, not an independent measurement.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use protein sequence or network features to predict which proteins show two-peaked (bimodal) abundance across tumours.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per protein quantified in CPTAC tumours, about 2401 of them labelled bimodal according to the abstract; the total protein count is unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a protein is bimodal. The answer comes from the authors' own statistical model fitted to CPTAC mass-spectrometry abundances, not from a separate measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Oncology target teams could flag proteins that split patients into high and low groups. But the label is a computed statistic, so even a successful model would only copy the authors' method.

label_elsewhere.sources: None found. Bimodality calls appear only in this paper, and its release was not retrievable.
label_elsewhere.why: No external bimodality labels were found to validate against.

ml_idea: Considered: predict proteomic bimodality from ESM-2 sequence embeddings plus network features. Rejected because the label is model-derived from the expression data and the paper's calls are not released.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because Part A failed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find a released supplementary table of per-protein bimodality calls. None was found through Europe PMC, Zenodo or the authors' GitHub.

verdict_reason: Fails A1, A2 and A8. The bimodal label is the authors' statistical-model output computed from the same CPTAC abundance data, and no released table of calls was found (no PMCID, empty GitHub repo). The underlying CPTAC data is open but needs no part of this paper.
